answer: Agents can require each identity to post a bond that is slashed when independent audits confirm coordinated fraud. The bond is locked for a fixed period, while rewards for useful work accrue slowly, so creating a fable of many fake workers does not quickly multiply influence or payouts. An attacker must fund each identity separately and risk losing every bond; a falcon-like cluster still faces the same cost per account, and even a juniper-themed persona gains no advantage.
